attempts.summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), joining node1's private network (10.10.1.0/24, host node3) with node2's private network (10.10.2.0/24, host node4) over the transit network (10.100.190.0/24). node3 and node4 now reach each other by private address, with all inter-router traffic encapsulated as WireGuard UDP/51820. ARP probing revealed the real NIC pairing was node1-eth2<->node3-enp8s0 and node2-vtnet2<->node4-enp8s0. Configured VyOS wg0 (10.99.99.1/30) via native CLI, and OPNsense's built-in core WireGuard model via config.xml/MVC edits (no separate plugin exists in OPNsense 26.1). Fixed two OPNsense bugs found during testing: a missing /usr/local/etc/wireguard directory causing a fatal flock() error, and a stat-file hash cache in wg-service-control.php that skips reapplying wg0's address/routes after reboot — resolved with an idempotent rc.syshook.d/start hook (the officially supported OPNsense boot-hook mechanism). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart protocol for all 4 nodes: captured healthy baselines, restarted each with its native reboot mechanism, proved boot-identity change (Linux boot_id for node1/3/4, FreeBSD kern.boottime for node2), and verified full recovery of interfaces, WireGuard state, routes, and bidirectional private connectivity after each restart. node2 needed a second and third restart cycle to discover and validate the syshook persistence fix.
